one_line: A craftable little soda-can robot that chirps with a bike-horn sound and can have reagents injected into the soda can inside it.
player_facing_mechanics: Craft the Little Soda Robot from a soda can, a proximity sensor and a right robot arm in the robot category.
The bot holds a soda can (a default soda can is auto-created if none supplied) and displays an overlay matching that can's icon.
Chirps (plays a bike-horn/smoke-detector sound) on its own via AI, with a 1-minute cooldown.
Each chirp has a 5% chance to destroy its buzzer, after which it can no longer chirp and the holder sees 'Your buzzer gives out!'.
Examine shows 'Reagents can be injected into it' to holders of the research scanner trait.
Behaves as a basic bot: responds to summon, salutes authority, patrols via beacons, and randomly uses its honk/chirp ability.
tg_systems_used: basic mob AI controllers / planning subtrees (respond_to_summon, salute_authority, use_mob_ability/random_honk, find_patrol_beacon)
data_only_parts: The crafting recipe stat block (reqs, parts, time, category, result).
The chirp action's name, desc, button icons, cooldown_time and click_to_activate flag.
logic_parts: Initialize: create_reagents(30), instantiate/grant the chirp action, wire the post-honk callback and blackboard key.
on_chirped: visible_message + 5% prob roll that breaks the buzzer.
add_soda_overlay: locate or create the soda can in contents and add a mutable_appearance overlay.
CheckParts: add the soda overlay after construction parts are assigned.
chirp Activate: playsound, invoke post_honk_callback, StartCooldown.
chirp IsAvailable/break_buzzer/Destroy: gate availability on buzzer_broken and null the callback on destroy.
examine override adding the reagent-injection notice for research scanner holders.
port_notes: This is a mostly self-contained NPC that maps cleanly to SS14: the mob becomes an entity prototype with a Sprite, a container/solution for the injected reagents, and an NPC component; the AI subtrees map to an NPC behaviour system (Utility/HTN or a blackboard-driven FSM); the chirp becomes an Action or an NPC ability invoked on a timer. The crafting recipe translates to a Construction/recipe prototype, and the soda-can overlay maps to a visual layer or a sprite-overlay component. Design questions a human must answer: whether the internal soda can should be a real spawned entity or a stored prototype, how reagent injection is exposed (interaction verb/UI) versus the BYOND trait check, and whether the 5% buzzer break should be a random server event or a data-driven chance.
